To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
okenone is a novel C50carotenoid with an aromatic ring system and a 2,3,2',3'-diepoxy-2,3'-dihydro structure.

okenone and rhodopinal are cross-conjugated, that okenone is an aryl ketone, that okenal is an aryl alcohol and that the C50carotenoid dehydrogenans is a C40carotenoid with two C5isoprene units attached to C40.

(a) okenone is the first example of an aryl ketone in nature and that (b) the rhodopinals are the first examples of cross-conjugated C50carotenoid hydrocarbons, the latter containing the 2,6,6'-triene and the 2,4,4,6,6,8-hexatriene systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis of the carotenoid skeleton and its modifications, with the introduction of substituent groups, and with the formation of carotenoid glycosides.
carotenoids of the photosynthetic bacteria Rhodopseudomonas spheroides and Rhodopseudomons palustris.
the biosynthesis of carotenes and xanthophylls in photosynthetic bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all carotenoids of these photosynthetic bacteria are derived from the common precursor, 3,4-dehydrolycopene.
the biosynthesis of carotenes and xanthophylls in photosynthetic bacteria is a highly complex process, involving a series of reactions, some of them still not fully clarified.

all carotenoids of the photosynthetic bacteria are derived from the C40compound 1, which in turn is derived from the C20compound farnesyl pyrophosphate (2), by way of a C30compound, 3, 3-hydroxy-C30, 4-keto-3,4-dihydro-C30, 1,4-dihy-dro-2-C30 and 1,4,2-trihydro-C30compounds
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the carotenoid biosynthesis in photosynthetic bacteria is very similar to that in higher plants and algae, with the exception that the first cyclization step is blocked.
the carotenoids are formed from a C20isoprenoid unit by condensation with C5isoprene units and subsequent cyclisation.

the carotenoids are biosynthesized from mevalonate, which is condensed to the C40hydrocarbon geranylgeraniol (I) by way of the C5isoprenoid pyrophosphate intermediates farnesyl pyrophosphate (III) and geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (IV).
